subject: anaesthesia
title: Volatile Agents: Halothane Hepatitis, Isoflurane Steal, and Sevoflurane Metabolism

steps.title: Halothane Hepatitis Pathogenesis
steps.tx: **Halothane hepatitis autoimmune mechanism** represents an immune-mediated centrilobular liver necrosis triggered by oxidative hepatic metabolism via cytochrome P450 2E1 (CYP2E1). Up to 20 percent of inhaled halothane is metabolized into reactive trifluoroacetyl chloride, which binds covalently to hepatocyte microsomal proteins. These neoantigens elicit anti-trifluoroacetyl antibodies upon repeated exposure, precipitating fulminant hepatic failure with an 80 percent case fatality rate.

steps.title: Halothane Hepatitis Risk Factors
steps.tx: **Risk factors for halothane-induced hepatitis** include repeated halothane exposures within an interval of under three months, female gender (female-to-male ratio of two to one), middle age, obesity, and underlying genetic predisposition to autoimmune reactivity. Children are remarkably resistant to fulminant autoimmune injury because immature hepatic CYP2E1 activity generates far fewer trifluoroacetylated protein adducts.

steps.title: Isoflurane and Coronary Steal
steps.tx: **Coronary steal phenomenon with isoflurane** arises because isoflurane is a potent direct arteriolar vasodilator of small resistance vessels (arterioles under 100 micrometers in diameter). In patients with critical coronary artery stenosis, isoflurane dilates healthy collateral arterioles supplying non-ischemic myocardium, diverting blood flow away from fixed stenotic channels and precipitating subendocardial ischemia, though modern clinical practice minimizes this risk by maintaining mean arterial pressure.

points: Arterioles distal to fixed atheroma are already maximally dilated

right.title: Isoflurane Arteriolar Vasodilation
points: Dilates resistance vessels in adjacent non-stenotic myocardial beds

steps.title: Metabolism Rates Across Volatiles
steps.tx: **Metabolic degradation rates of volatile agents** dictate organ toxicity risk based on the percentage of absorbed drug cleared by hepatic biotransformation: halothane is metabolized extensively (15 to 20 percent), sevoflurane undergoes intermediate metabolism (3 to 5 percent), isoflurane undergoes minimal degradation (0.2 percent), and desflurane is virtually inert (0.02 percent), making desflurane incapable of generating significant trifluoroacetylated neoantigens.

steps.title: Sevoflurane Fluoride and Nephrotoxicity
steps.tx: **Inorganic fluoride release from sevoflurane** metabolism via hepatic CYP2E1 yields free fluoride ions and hexafluoroisopropanol. Historical methoxyflurane anaesthesia established that serum inorganic fluoride concentrations exceeding 50 micromoles per liter induce dose-dependent vasopressin-resistant high-output polyuric nephrotoxicity. However, sevoflurane undergoes rapid pulmonary clearance, so intra-renal fluoride release remains insufficient to produce clinical renal injury.

points: Fifty percent metabolized into free inorganic fluoride

right.title: Sevoflurane Clinical Safety
points: Only 3 to 5 percent metabolized into fluoride ions
Fluoride levels transiently peak around 20 to 30 umol/L
Zero concentrating defect; rapid pulmonary elimination

steps.title: Sevoflurane Mask Induction Advantages
steps.tx: **Pediatric inhalational induction with sevoflurane** represents the clinical gold standard for smooth inhalational induction in uncooperative children. Sevoflurane exhibits a pleasant, non-pungent, sweet odor that causes zero airway irritation, coughing, breath-holding, or laryngospasm at concentrations up to 8 percent, while its low blood-gas partition coefficient (0.65) ensures rapid loss of consciousness within 60 to 90 seconds.

steps.title: Arrhythmogenic Myocardial Sensitization
steps.tx: **Myocardial sensitization to catecholamines** varies sharply between volatile anaesthetics: halothane sensitizes ventricular myocardium to endogenous and exogenous adrenaline by disrupting Purkinje fiber conduction and prolonging refractoriness, setting a strict safe submucosal adrenaline infiltration limit of 1 microgram per kilogram (under 10 milliliters of 1:100,000 solution). Isoflurane and sevoflurane tolerate three to five times higher adrenaline doses without ventricular dysrhythmias.

steps.title: Emergence Agitation with Sevoflurane
steps.tx: **Emergence delirium with sevoflurane** occurs in up to 30 to 40 percent of young pediatric patients recovering rapidly from brief ambulatory procedures. Children present with inconsolable crying, thrashing, motor disorientation, and unresponsiveness, caused by rapid awakening in an unfamiliar environment before sensory analgesia is established. Premedication with oral midazolam, intravenous fentanyl, or alpha-2 agonists like dexmedetomidine effectively suppresses this agitation.

left.title: Clinical Emergence Delirium
points: Restless thrashing, inconsolable crying, non-purposeful kicking
Presents within the first 15 minutes of PACU admission
